specialization: Technical SEO, information architecture, content strategy, accessibility, analytics

findings.exact_claim: Every probed production URL, including pages with HTML <meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">, also sends HTTP X-Robots-Tag: index, follow. Observed 2026-09-02 on /clinics, /clinics/miami, /glossary/a1c, /404, /robots.txt, /sitemap-0.xml, /llms.txt, /api/health.
findings.user_safety_impact: Indirect. If a crawler prefers the HTTP header over HTML meta, noindex clinic/glossary/404 pages could enter the index with unverified clinic claims.
findings.search_business_impact: Index bloat and mixed signals on the crawl-budget-constrained site. Google documents that conflicting robots rules resolve to the more restrictive rule, so noindex should still win in Googlebot; other crawlers may differ. Header still advertises index on assets that should never be indexed.
findings.proposed_wording: Remove the sitewide X-Robots-Tag: index, follow header. Set X-Robots-Tag only where it matches the HTML robots intent (noindex, follow on /clinics/*, noindex glossary terms, 404, APIs). Do not send index on XML/txt endpoints.
findings.effort_dependencies: Vercel header change; production deploy on main; URL Inspection sample after deploy
findings.acceptance_test: curl -sI a noindex page shows X-Robots-Tag: noindex, follow or omits X-Robots-Tag; HTML meta remains noindex, follow; an indexable peptide page has no conflicting noindex header.

findings.exact_claim: Every peptide dossier emits schema.org Drug with hardcoded legalStatus "Research use only - not FDA approved for human use" and administrationRoute "Subcutaneous injection", including FDA-approved products such as semaglutide (Ozempic/Wegovy/Rybelsus).
findings.user_safety_impact: High. Machine-readable markup tells crawlers and assistants that approved medicines are research-only and injectable-only (Rybelsus is oral). Opposite error also exists: research peptides are typed as Drug.
findings.search_business_impact: Rich-result ineligibility or misleading knowledge-panel facts; YMYL trust damage if Google surfaces schema text.
supporting_sources: src/layouts/DossierLayout.astro DrugSchema call legalStatus and administrationRoute
src/content/peptides/semaglutide.mdx summary: FDA-approved for T2D, obesity, CVD risk, MASH; aliases include Rybelsus
findings.proposed_wording: Emit Drug (or Drug + MedicalWebPage) only when regulatoryStatus.status is approved; set legalStatus from that field and labels; set administrationRoute from labeled product facts (do not hardcode subcutaneous). For research-only compounds use ScholarlyArticle/MedicalWebPage without Drug.legalStatus 'research use only' copied onto approved drugs. Never contradict visible dossier text.
findings.acceptance_test: View-source on /peptides/semaglutide does not contain 'Research use only - not FDA approved for human use'. Rybelsus/oral is not described as subcutaneous-only. Research-only peptides are not marked FDA-approved.

findings.exact_claim: Templated FAQ: `${name} has ${cityClinics.length > 0 ? cityClinics.length : 'multiple'} peptide therapy clinics...` When a city has zero clinics the schema and visible FAQ still say 'multiple'. FAQ also states 'Verified listings in our directory have been vetted' and 'Initial consultations typically range from $100-$300'. Inventory: 12 cities with zero clinics; 52/52 clinic websites are example.com placeholders; 50 verifiedListing true.
findings.user_safety_impact: High. Users may treat placeholder clinics as vetted providers. Price range is unsourced. 'Multiple clinics' on empty cities is false.
findings.search_business_impact: Doorway-style city FAQs. Pages are HTML-noindex (good) but still crawlable; FAQPage schema remains. If header indexing wins, these could rank.
supporting_sources: Live 2026-09-02 /clinics/miami 200, meta robots noindex, follow, jsonld FAQPage
findings.proposed_wording: Do not emit FAQPage for cities with no independently verified clinics. Do not say 'multiple' when count is 0. Do not say listings are vetted unless a documented verification protocol and last-checked date exist. Do not state consultation prices without a sourced range. Keep noindex until records have real official websites.
findings.effort_dependencies: clinics/[city].astro; clinic MDX data quality (Audit C)
findings.acceptance_test: A zero-clinic city page has no FAQ claiming multiple clinics and no FAQPage JSON-LD. verifiedListing is not true when website is example.com.

findings.exact_claim: 181/269 comparison MDX bodies are under 200 words (median 182). 265/269 metaTitle values are '{A} vs {B}: Which Has Better Evidence?'. 73/269 metaDescriptions contain a leaked YAML marker '>- Citations and data reviewed.'. 76/269 include a templated 'Can A and B be used together?' FAQ with the same unknown-combination answer.
findings.user_safety_impact: Medium. Combination FAQs discuss co-use of research peptides without evidence. Templated 'better evidence' titles overclaim.
findings.search_business_impact: Google scaled-content and doorway policies (Search Central spam policies, accessed 2026-09-02) target large sets of similar pages created to rank for query variants. 269 indexable comparison URLs consume crawl budget. Historical GSC 2026-07-24 noted most URLs never received an impression — not current, but the URL count has not shrunk.
supporting_sources: node count 2026-09-02: yamlLeak 73, better 265, comboFaq 76 of 269
contradictory_sources: 84 comparisons have ≥500 body words, including tirzepatide-vs-semaglutide which cites SURMOUNT-5 PMID 40353578
findings.proposed_wording: Keep only comparisons that add unique trial-level contrast. Drop thin pages from the sitemap, apply noindex, follow, and 301 to the stronger peptide dossier or a single GLP-1 comparison hub. Fix YAML-leaked descriptions. Stop the 'Which Has Better Evidence?' stamp. Net URL count must fall.
findings.effort_dependencies: redirect map; sitemap filter; crawl-graph check
findings.acceptance_test: npm run graph:check passes; comparison URL count in sitemap is the retained set only; sample thin URL 301s; no metaDescription contains '>-'.

findings.exact_claim: Each peptide-condition URL is a programmatic page whose unique body is mainly condition.researchSummary plus PMID chips, wrapped in chrome. Graph (local dist 2026-09-02): 206 pages at click-depth 3 (largest depth bucket after 2). Template metaDescription is generated: 'Evidence-based research on {name} for {condition}...'. Article schema dateModified is the parent dossier date.
findings.user_safety_impact: Medium. Condition pages can imply indication-like pairings for unapproved peptides.
findings.search_business_impact: 295 extra indexable URLs at depth 3. Crawl budget binding constraint. Overlap with /conditions/{slug} and dossier sections.
contradictory_sources: DossierLayout comments that condition links were added to prevent orphan islands
findings.proposed_wording: Prefer in-dossier condition sections with fragment URLs. If pages remain, noindex, follow + sitemap exclude until a page has unique sourced prose beyond a short summary. Do not add more condition URLs.
findings.effort_dependencies: astro.config SITEMAP_EXCLUDE; getStaticPaths; internal links from dossiers must not 404
findings.acceptance_test: Sitemap peptide-condition count drops; graph:check has no new orphans; retained pages have unique researchSummary substantially longer than chrome.

findings.exact_claim: 36 identical slugs exist in both blog and guide collections (the entire guide set). Examples: what-is-bpc-157, what-is-semaglutide, what-is-ozempic, what-are-glp1-agonists. Live 2026-09-02: /blog/what-is-bpc-157 and /guide/what-is-bpc-157 both 200, both indexable (metaRobots null).
findings.user_safety_impact: Low-medium. Readers may land on the thinner or older of two near-duplicate explainers.
findings.search_business_impact: Site-diversity systems generally cap same-site listings. Two URLs split ranking signals for the same 'what is X' query. Guide lastUpdated for BPC-157 is 2026-01-19; blog was rewritten 2026-09-01 to point at the guide — slug still cannibalizes.
supporting_sources: src/content/blog/what-is-bpc-157.mdx excerpt states beginner definition lives on the guide
findings.proposed_wording: Keep /guide/what-is-{x} as the definition URL. Change blog slugs to non-competing titles (as BPC-157 blog title already did) and 301 leftover what-is blog URLs to the guide. One indexable URL per definition intent.
findings.acceptance_test: GET /blog/what-is-bpc-157 returns 301 to /guide/what-is-bpc-157 or a non-competing slug; sitemap contains one URL for that intent.

findings.exact_claim: This branch's vercel.json 301s /blog/2025-glp1-year-review → /peptides/semaglutide and /calculator/reconstitution/tesamorelin → /peptides/tesamorelin. Live production 2026-09-02: both URLs are 200 and in the live sitemap (year-review lastmod 2025-12-22). Live sitemap also lists other LIVE-NOT-IN-REPO blogs this branch would 301 to /blog.

supporting_sources: vercel.json redirects for 2025-glp1-year-review and tesamorelin calculator
LIVE-PROBES.json and audit-b live probes 2026-09-02 status 200
findings.proposed_wording: Do not merge feat/scoring-and-freshness to main as a sync side effect. Decide per-URL: retire (301+sitemap drop) or keep. Document the production redirect table separately from this branch.
findings.effort_dependencies: production vercel.json vs this file; sitemap rebuild on main
findings.acceptance_test: A written URL disposition list; live HEAD matches the intended status for each contested URL.

findings.exact_claim: Organization JSON-LD sets logo https://www.pepcodex.com/logo.png and sameAs: []. Live 2026-09-02: logo.png returns 404. Footer links Instagram https://www.instagram.com/pepcodex/ which is absent from sameAs. Schema is emitted on every page via BaseLayout, including 404.
findings.user_safety_impact: None.
findings.search_business_impact: Invalid logo URL in Organization/publisher ImageObject (ArticleSchema also uses logo.png). Knowledge-panel / sitelink eligibility weakened. Organization on 404 is unnecessary.

findings.exact_claim: Live llms.txt (2026-09-02) says last updated 2026-02-18, 'world's most comprehensive evidence-based peptide directory', '1,300+ pages covering 92 peptide dossiers, 279 comparisons, 215 glossary terms, 151 blog posts', and lists URLs with trailing slashes. Repo generator uses collection counts, forbids trailing slashes, and omits the superlative. Both files still call /directory the Clinic Directory (a coming-soon page).
findings.user_safety_impact: Low. LLM crawlers may cite inflated counts and hit 308s from trailing slashes.
findings.search_business_impact: Trailing-slash URLs cost redirect hops (trailingSlash: never). Superlative is unverifiable. Directory URL is a placeholder.
findings.proposed_wording: Deploy the repo generator. Replace 'Clinic Directory' with a label that matches the coming-soon page or omit until listings are real. Do not use 'world's most comprehensive'.
findings.acceptance_test: Live llms.txt date equals last production build date; zero trailing slashes; no superlative; counts match collections.

findings.exact_claim: Homepage canonical is https://www.pepcodex.com/ (trailing slash). Live sitemap loc is https://www.pepcodex.com (no slash). Config trailingSlash: 'never'. Homepage copy still says 'This volume / Issue Spring 2026' on 2026-09-02. Featured brief slugs include posts in REPO-NOT-IN-LIVE (semax-neuroprotection-stroke, semaglutide-vs-tirzepatide-2026, dsip-sleep-quality-study). Default meta description is the sitewide generic string.
findings.user_safety_impact: None.
findings.search_business_impact: Homepage canonical vs sitemap mismatch. Seasonal branding is stale. Featured links may 404 or point at un-sitemapped URLs depending on which tree is live. Web search 2026-09-02 still retrieved pepcodex.com/blog/semaglutide-vs-tirzepatide-2026.
findings.proposed_wording: Emit a single homepage URL consistently (prefer https://www.pepcodex.com with no slash, matching trailingSlash never). Remove or date-stamp volume copy. Feature only URLs that are 200 and sitemap-included on production.
findings.acceptance_test: Homepage canonical equals sitemap loc; featured hrefs all 200 and in sitemap-0.xml.

findings.exact_claim: Calculator inputs include 'Desired dose (mcg): the amount you want to draw per administration' and output 'Volume per dose'. Disclaimer says it is not a dosing tool. Live title: 'Tesamorelin Reconstitution Calculator: Research Tool'. This branch 301s the live URL to the dossier; production is 200. Competitors in SERP 2026-09-02 (peptidecalcs.com, peppal.app, pepzilla.app, rainbowpeptide.com) pair reconstitution with syringe-unit dosing presets for BPC-157/semaglutide.
findings.user_safety_impact: High if users treat volume-per-dose as a recommended dose. Tesamorelin is FDA-approved as Egrifta with manufacturer reconstitution instructions the page itself says are not interchangeable.
findings.search_business_impact: Reconstitution-calculator SERP is dominated by vendor/app dosing tools. Ranking there without tight educational framing is a YMYL risk, not a traffic opportunity to chase with more URLs.
supporting_sources: tesamorelin-reconstitution.mdx inputs and How to Use list
SERP 2026-09-02 US English web_search peptide reconstitution calculator
findings.proposed_wording: Keep at most the existing calculators. Rename 'desired dose' to 'example mass to convert'. Do not add peptide-specific dosing presets. Do not HowTo-schema injection steps. Prefer linking Egrifta label reconstitution for the approved product. Do not create additional calculator URLs.
findings.acceptance_test: Visible copy never says 'dose' as an instruction; no HowTo schema; no new /calculator URLs in sitemap.

findings.exact_claim: metaDescription: 'Preclinical repair peptide — no human trials yet. Updated Feb 2026.' Frontmatter sources.human: 2 and summary: 'A 2025 systematic review of 36 studies found only 1 clinical study.' lastUpdated: 2026-01-22.
findings.user_safety_impact: Medium. Snippet understates that some human data exist (still very limited). Date 'Updated Feb 2026' does not match lastUpdated January 22.
findings.search_business_impact: SERP snippet for a high-demand unapproved peptide is inaccurate. Independent 2026 coverage (STAT 2026-02-03; Psychology Today 2026-08-29) emphasizes Croatian-lab concentration and tiny human N — the dossier should match that caution, not a false 'zero trials' line.
findings.proposed_wording: Evidence-graded BPC-157 dossier: almost all published work is preclinical and concentrated in one research program; human studies are few, small, and not randomized. Not FDA-approved.
findings.acceptance_test: metaDescription does not say 'no human trials yet' while sources.human > 0; visible last updated matches lastUpdated.

findings.exact_claim: Footer and live llms.txt present /directory as the clinic directory. /directory is a 'Coming Soon' page (indexable, 200). /clinics is a populated city index with 60 city pages and is noindex. Nav does not link /clinics. Dual IA: an indexable empty promise and a noindex real list.
findings.user_safety_impact: Users following 'directory' never reach city listings; users on city pages see unverified cards.
findings.search_business_impact: Indexable coming-soon page wastes a crawl. Noindex listings still consume crawls because noindex does not save budget until sitemap exclusion (already true for /clinics) AND reduced internal links.
findings.proposed_wording: One public URL. Until listings are real, keep a single coming-soon page and do not describe it as a live verified directory. Keep city pages noindex and out of sitemap.
findings.acceptance_test: Only one clinic-directory URL is indexable; its visible H1 matches reality (coming soon or live listings, not both).

findings.exact_claim: GA4 gtag.js is injected in <head> whenever PUBLIC_GA_TRACKING_ID is set, with gtag('config') immediately. CookieConsent later calls gtag('consent','default',{analytics_storage:'denied'}) on DOMContentLoaded if no stored choice. Vercel Analytics inject() is not gated. Analytics checkbox defaults to checked. GSC/GA4 live pull is blocked (invalid_rapt). Historical note in project files: GA4 topline ~91% bots as of 2026-07.
findings.user_safety_impact: Privacy: analytics may fire before consent default. US is primary jurisdiction; GDPR claims in the component comment are not a US legal conclusion.
findings.search_business_impact: Cannot measure current impressions, CTR, or conversions. Historical GA4 is bot-contaminated. Search/business KPIs are BASELINE UNAVAILABLE as of 2026-09-02.
findings.proposed_wording: Load gtag with consent default denied in the same inline snippet before config. Gate Vercel Analytics on analytics consent. Repair ADC/rapt so npm run gsc:repull and ga4:pull work. Do not treat 2026-07 GA4 sessions as human traffic.
findings.effort_dependencies: Google account reauth; consent snippet order
findings.acceptance_test: Network tab shows no google-analytics collect before consent; gsc:whoami succeeds; bot filter documented in GA4.

findings.exact_claim: About page has no named person, credentials, or reviewer. ArticleSchema author is Organization PepCodex. Blog author string is 'PepCodex Research Team'. Editorial policy claims 'All content passes editorial review before publication' and 'Every cited source is verified' without a public reviewer name or correction log. No author URL or Person schema.
findings.user_safety_impact: Readers cannot identify who is accountable for health-adjacent claims.
findings.search_business_impact: Google helpful-content / health YMYL guidance expects identifiable expertise. Organization-only authorship on drug-like pages is a ranking-quality gap, not a metric I can quantify without GSC.
findings.proposed_wording: On /about, name the responsible editor(s) with real bios and a medical-reviewer disclosure if used. Add a dated corrections list on /editorial-policy. Do not invent credentials. Do not add dozens of author URLs.
findings.acceptance_test: About names at least one real person; Article pages that make medical claims either cite that person as reviewer or remain Organization with a visible 'no individual medical reviewer' disclosure.

findings.exact_claim: Page-level statement: 'The statements and information on this website have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The content is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.' This is applied as a sitewide frame even though the library includes FDA-approved drug dossiers (semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide, tesamorelin).
findings.user_safety_impact: A blanket DSHEA-style notice on pages about approved drugs can confuse readers about which compounds are actually approved.
findings.search_business_impact: Trust mismatch: schema says research-only (B-002) while dossiers say approved while FDA-notice says nothing was evaluated.
findings.proposed_wording: Distinguish: (1) FDA-approved labeled products vs (2) compounded copies vs (3) research-only peptides. Do not put a supplement-style 'not evaluated' banner over approved-drug dossiers. Expert legal review required; this is not a legal conclusion.
findings.acceptance_test: FDA notice page explicitly separates approved vs unapproved content; approved dossiers do not inherit supplement-style 'not evaluated' as the primary regulatory fact.

findings.exact_claim: Unknown path returns 200-class HTML 404 with title Page Not Found, canonical https://www.pepcodex.com/404, meta robots noindex, follow, and X-Robots-Tag index, follow. Status code from fetch was 404.
